newsitem.title: JAPAN: Greenspan sidesteps queries on rates, currencies.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan sidesteps queries on rates, currencies.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Monday dodged queries on interest rates and currencies, telling Japanese bankers he was well-schooled in the art of being "cryptic" and "incomprehensible".

"The answer to that sort of question I usually do behind closed doors and make certain that there are three locks on each door," Greenspan said when asked about the possibility of a "triple depreciation" in which U.S. stocks, bonds and the dollar all fell simultaneously.

"I apologise, I'm just really not able to respond to markets, interest rates and all related types of issues because I've been taught by previous central bankers to be terribly cryptic, and when addressing such issues to be utterly incomprehensible."
He similarly declined to comment on currencies.
Greenspan, who as chairman of the Fed heads the U.S. central banking system, is in Tokyo for two days of meetings with Japanese financial and monetary authorities.

In a speech to the Federation of Bankers' Associations of Japan, Greenspan said central banks needed to prevent big financial market disruptions but not stop private institutions from taking risks even if doing so resulted in losses or failures.
Japan is preparing for a five-year "Big Bang" to liberalise its financial markets by 2001 to help Tokyo compete with London and New York.
